title: ADU rule file
description: One file per place or per bill. Every rule value is a leaf: {value, section, url, verified_on, confidence, note, mode}. null with confidence unverified means not confirmed, so the resolver falls back. null with verified or secondary means the source sets no single number. mode tells a reform layer how to combine with the place: set replaces, at_least is a floor the town may not go under, at_most is a cap the town may not go over. Feet and square feet.

county.description: County name without the word County, e.g. Lehigh. Town files only.

municipality_type.description: As in the Census name. Home rule places keep their Census type (Bethel Park and Monroeville are municipality).

geoid.description: 2020 Census county subdivision GEOID (state 42 + county 3 + cousub 5). Must exist in towns_index.json.

code_url.description: Link to the zoning chapter as published online.

code_current_through.description: The date the online code says it is current to. null when the publisher shows none.

code_current_through_note.description: The currency line as the publisher shows it, e.g. 'Current through Ord. 2025-4, adopted 6-2-2025'.

geoid_aliases.description: Other Census county subdivision GEOIDs of the same place, e.g. the part of a city in a second county (Bethlehem, Lehigh part 4207706088). Lookups by these find this file.

code_caution.description: A caution about the code text itself, shown with every answer: the online code is a placeholder, or amendments exist that were not seen.

adu.description: Town files: what the code calls an ADU and how it treats one, each cited. status not_addressed means the code has no ADU text. Then cite the nearest sections (accessory uses, family, two-family) in approval.path.

scope_districts.description: The ADU rule reaches only these districts or overlays. Elsewhere status_outside applies.

approval.description: How a qualifying ADU is approved, and the path when the lot does not qualify.

unlisted_use_path.description: Path for a use the code does not list (for example a special exception for uses not provided for, Lancaster 300-17, Hempfield 87-186). Not where the code bars unlisted uses.

eligibility.description: Which lots qualify. building_types uses detached, semi_detached, attached.

min_lot_share_of_district.description: The lot needs only this share of the district minimum lot (Manheim: 0.9).

requires_conforming_lot.description: true when the code ties the ADU to a lot that meets the district minimum lot (a conforming lot). Without it, a lot below the district minimum is shown as a possible nonconforming lot, not barred.

historic_test.description: The town's own test for the historic path in plain words (for example on the Historic Resources Map). With it the resolver reads the lot fact historic_resource, not the Philadelphia inputs.

districts_in_doubt.description: Districts that list the ADU while the ADU section names other districts. The tool says: listed, ask. Not allowed as a plain answer.

types_allowed_historic.description: Forms allowed on the historic path, when they differ from types_allowed.

size.description: Floor area of the ADU. When a reform layer gives both max_sqft and max_share_of_house as at_least, the floor is the lesser of the two.

max_share_internal.description: Share cap for a unit inside or attached to the house, when it differs from max_share_of_house (which then holds for a unit in an accessory building).

max_sqft_internal.description: Floor area cap for a unit inside or attached to the house, when it differs from max_sqft.

max_sqft_accessory_building.description: Floor area cap for a unit in a detached or accessory building (new, garage conversion, over a garage), when it differs from max_sqft.

max_share_accessory_building.description: Share cap for a unit in an accessory building, when it differs from max_share_of_house.

envelope.description: Height and distances for a new ADU structure. max_height_ft is the limit for a detached or garage ADU. The last three are building code distances to a lot line or to the line between two buildings.

max_height_garage_ft.description: Height cap for a garage (garage conversion, unit over a garage) when it differs from max_height_ft.

height_capped_at_house.description: true when an accessory building may not be taller than the house (Lower Paxton 203-313H).

accessory_height_applies.description: false when the file says no accessory height rule reaches an ADU, so the district height applies. Leave out when unknown.

district_yards_bind_accessory.description: true when the code makes accessory buildings meet the district (principal) yards. Otherwise a detached unit takes the envelope yards and an attached unit the district yards.

accessory_cap_districts.description: Districts where accessory_structure_max_sqft applies, when the code limits it (Lower Paxton: residential lots under 2 acres).

accessory_floor_area_total_sqft.description: Lot-wide total floor area of all accessory buildings, an existing garage included (Warminster 27-1786.1.G, 500 sq ft of ground floor area). Not a per-building cap.

accessory_structure_threshold_sqft.description: Above this floor area an accessory building needs a special exception or other approval (Norristown 320-232A(2), 600 sq ft). Not a cap. Use accessory_structure_max_sqft only for a hard cap.

unit_within_building_envelope.description: true when the unit must sit inside the building envelope (outside the district yards), so no alley rear default applies (Warminster 27-1793).

max_height_stories.description: Accessory building height in stories, when the code gives stories.

accessory_structure_max_share.description: Every accessory structure: at most this share of the house, beside accessory_structure_max_sqft (whichever is less).

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.description: The general accessory structure height, when the ADU text sets its own height in max_height_ft.

accessory_cap_binds_adu.description: Whether the general accessory structure caps (accessory_structure_max_sqft, _max_share, _max_height_ft) also bind a unit in an accessory building. true: the lesser applies. false: the ADU text replaces them. null: not settled, both are shown.

front_yard_barred.description: true when an accessory building may not stand in the front yard (between the house and the street), a bar rather than a setback number. Put any exception in the note (for example 100 ft from the street).

use.description: Who may live there and how many units.

parking.description: Extra off-street spaces for the ADU.

total_on_site.description: Total off-street spaces the lot needs with the ADU (house plus ADU), when the code states it.

reading.description: When the parking rule has more than one reading, state them here in plain words (e.g. '2 in total, or 4 if the apartment counts as a unit').

spaces_per_resident.description: Spaces per resident of the unit, when the code counts residents. spaces_required stays null.

statewide.description: pa_statewide.json only. What applies in every Pennsylvania town, one cited text item per key. value is a short plain statement.

districts.description: Per base district standards. Keys are district codes as mapped (e.g. RSA-5, R1D-L).

leaf_num.description: A number in feet or square feet. null means no single number. See confidence.

leaf_overlay_bars.description: Overlays that bar ADUs. districts null means every base district. council_districts and wards say where the overlay applies, so a lot can be placed by council district or ward when no overlay map is at hand.

district.description: Base district standards that bind an accessory structure.

separation_ft.description: Minimum distance between dwellings on a lot in this district, when the code sets one.

accessory_setback_front_ft.description: Accessory building yard in this district, when it differs from the town-wide envelope value.

accessory_setback_side_ft.description: Accessory building yard in this district, when it differs from the town-wide envelope value.

accessory_setback_rear_ft.description: Accessory building yard in this district, when it differs from the town-wide envelope value.

principal_max_stories.description: Principal building height in stories, when the code gives stories. Fill it beside principal_max_height_ft, and alone when the code gives no feet figure.

leaf_adu_status.description: How the town code treats an ADU. family_only: occupants must be family or caregivers. conversion_only: only inside an existing building. not_addressed: the code has no ADU text.

leaf_district_paths.description: Approval path by zoning district, when it differs from approval.path. A district row's adu_path wins over this list.

term.description: The code's name for the unit under this district listing, when it differs from adu.term. The town-wide conditions still apply.

leaf_gates.description: Conditions that limit where or how an ADU is allowed. Scope: applies_to (ADU types, null = all), districts and building_types (null = everywhere), when (always, historic, not_historic). test names the lot fact that decides it (has_alley, has_accessory_building), null when no lot fact can. effect bars: in scope and the test fails (or there is no test), those types are not allowed. effect condition: shown to the user, never decides. lot_sqft_at_least and lot_sqft_below compare the lot area with value.

value.description: Threshold for test lot_sqft_at_least (met when the lot is at least this) or lot_sqft_below (met when the lot is under this).

not_districts.description: The gate applies everywhere except these districts or overlays.

bill_overrides.description: true when HB 2186 would remove this condition (for example a connection or employee-only rule). Family, owner and lot rules are already treated so.

leaf_alternatives.description: Other ways to add a second unit that are not an ADU (two-family conversion, duplex, second principal dwelling). Never counted as the ADU being allowed.

adu_listing.description: true when the code itself calls this an accessory dwelling unit under another listing (its own path and standards). It is shown as an ADU under another listing, not as 'not an ADU'.

land_development.description: true when the path also needs land development (subdivision and land development) plan approval, so it is never a plain zoning permit.

min_units.description: Units the path needs on the lot in all, when more than two (for example a conversion to three or more units). Over two, it is not a path for one added unit.

min_lot_is_tract.description: true when min_lot_sqft is a tract size (the development tract), not the lot of one house.

leaf_yard_tiers.description: Yards that depend on lot size. Each tier: lot size range and the yards. The resolver picks the tier for the lot, or says the yards depend on the lot tier.

leaf_labels.description: Display names for ADU forms, keyed by type, e.g. {"detached_new": "unit joined to the house by a breezeway"}.

leaf_form_paths.description: Approval path by ADU form, when a form's path differs from approval.path (for example a garage conversion by special exception where a unit in the house is by right). The resolver uses the more demanding of the two. Not applied under a state bill.

leaf_height_where.description: An accessory height that holds only where the building sits (for example 24 ft outside the principal building setbacks, 15 ft inside them). envelope.max_height_ft keeps the height the tool shows. Each item is shown as a condition.

leaf_status_by_form.description: ADU status for some forms when it differs from adu.status (for example a detached unit expressly prohibited where a unit in the house is not addressed). Forms left out take adu.status.
